newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore signs landmark gas deal with Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore signs landmark gas deal with Indonesia.

text.p: A subsidiary of Sembawang Corp said on Wednesday a consortium it leads has signed a landmark agreement with Indonesian state-owned Pertamina to import natural gas from the West Natuna field.

Sembawang Engineering and Construction Pte Ltd (SembEC) said in a statement the agreement, the first between the two countries, would make Indonesia the largest supplier of piped gas to Singapore in 2000.
Singapore now imports 150 million natural standard cubic feet per day of natural gas from Malaysia via a pipeline.
SembEC said its consortium included EDB Investments Pte Ltd and Tuas Power Pte Ltd, both owned by the Singapore government.

Under the agreement, Pertamina will supply 325 million standard cubic feet of natural gas per day for 22 years beginning in 2000 via a 480-km pipeline from Indonesia to Singapore's southwestern Jurong island.

"The signing of this letter of agreement with Pertamina is a significant milestone both in the planned development of SembEC's cogeneration capabilities and in the development of Jurong Island as a petrochemical hub," SembEC chief Tan Mong said in the statement.
The final agreement is expected to be signed later this year.
SembEC plans to use the gas to fuel a planned 600 megawatt power plant.
Tuas Power, a newcomer to a Singapore power sector due to be liberalised in two years, will use the gas for a new 1,200 megawatt plant expected to start up in April 1999.
SembEC said the natural gas would also be offered to petrochemical firms moving onto Jurong Island, designed as a centre for the industry.
A SembEC official said the gas would also be offered to rival Singapore Power, the current monopoly power provider in Singapore.
The official said SembEC would lead a separate consortium to build the pipeline. She gave no further details
